---
title: bc.raw
---
## Broadcasted Byte and Relational Operations on Raw Arrays {.unnumbered}


### Description

The <code>bc.raw()</code> function
performs broadcasted byte- and relational operations
on arrays of type <code>raw</code>. <br />
<br />
For bit-wise operations, use [bc.bit](bc.bit.qmd). <br />
For logical operations, use [bc.b](bc.b.qmd) <br />
<br />



### Usage

<pre><code class='language-R'>bc.raw(x, y, op, ...)

## S4 method for signature 'ANY'
bc.raw(x, y, op)
</code></pre>


### Arguments

<table>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="x">x</code>, <code id="y">y</code></td>
<td>
conformable raw vectors or arrays.
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="op">op</code></td>
<td>
a single string, giving the operator. <br />
Supported byte operators: pmin, pmax, diff. <br />
The &quot;diff&quot; operator performs the byte equivalent of <code>abs(x - y)</code>. <br />
Supported relational operators: ==, !=, &lt;, &gt;, &lt;=, &gt;=.
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="...">...</code></td>
<td>
further arguments passed to or from methods. <br /> <br />
</td></tr>
</table>


### Value

For the byte operators: <br />
A array of type <code>raw</code>,
as a result of the broadcasted byte operation. <br />
<br />
For relational operators: <br />
A logical array as a result of the broadcasted relational comparison. <br />
<br />



### Examples
```{r, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, eval=TRUE, collapse = TRUE, comment = NA}
library("broadcast")

x.dim <- c(4:2)
x.len <- prod(x.dim)
x.data <- as.raw(0:10)
y.data <- as.raw(10:0)
x <- array(x.data, x.dim)
y <- array(y.data, c(4,1,1))

bc.raw(x, y, "==")
bc.raw(x, y, "!=")
bc.raw(x, y, "<")
bc.raw(x, y, ">")
bc.raw(x, y, "<=")
bc.raw(x, y, ">=")



```
